source_cleanup.scope: All source, integration, and candidate worktrees and their local branches for this change

deviations.reason: The approved verification invokes root contract tasks and fixed official generators, but T-02 originally made Taskfile.yml and dependency lock manifests read-only
deviations.resolution: Serialize the minimal root task registrations and exact task-set assertion, exact Go/pnpm dependencies, and the exact @redocly/cli@2.48.0 release-age allowlist under T-02 without weakening policy or changing the Spec/ADR

deviations.reason: The first review proved that the fragment template targets the pre-reconstruction UI directory and cannot represent multiple fragments owned by one target module
deviations.resolution: Keep T-02 writes inside its existing template and tooling paths, but make generated module metadata declare an explicit owner and the Spec-authoritative go-admin-plus-ui/packages/domains target; no future module source is written by T-02

deviations.reason: The existing public generate task invokes superseded generators, including an unmanaged swag executable that fails from a provisioned repository, and would otherwise split the public generation contract
deviations.resolution: Replace the public generate delegation with the canonical OpenAPI generator; legacy scripts remain read-only expand-phase inventory until their T-21 contraction owner removes them, but are no longer part of the public command plane

deviations.reason: T-05 requires app-shell to be a real workspace package with public exports, but its writable path list omitted the package manifest while allowing only src/core
deviations.resolution: Authorize only go-admin-plus-ui/packages/app-shell/package.json as a T-05 shared path; keep all other app-shell files outside src/core read-only

deviations.reason: ADR-011 requires runtime adapters under packages/adapters/{browser,desktop} and Apps to select rather than own adapters, but T-05 omitted adapter package paths
deviations.resolution: Authorize go-admin-plus-ui/packages/adapters/browser/** and only the desktop adapter package manifest; move the browser runtime implementation out of admin-web while reserving desktop adapter source for T-16

deviations.reason: T-06 clean preflight proved the canonical TypeScript client and contract tool root still target the legacy go-admin-ui-plus workspace and each module fragment would rewrite the T-02 shared generated manifest
deviations.resolution: Reopen T-02, migrate the canonical API client/tool root to go-admin-plus-ui, and keep the shared manifest canonical-only while module outputs remain deterministically generated and checked from their fragments

deviations.reason: The precreated IAM workspace package manifests cannot expose or compile the Session slice without declaring public exports and direct API client, domain, and Vue dependencies
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the two IAM package manifests and the new workspace lockfile for exact Session exports and direct dependencies after T02-D04 is integrated

deviations.reason: Adding the planned canonical API client to the new workspace exposed a T-05 boundary assertion that hard-coded the previously discovered package count as 23
deviations.resolution: Reopen T-05 and replace only the brittle count with an explicit required package set while continuing to validate every discovered current and future package

deviations.reason: The first dual-axis review proved that T-06 requires typed Session policy from the T-03 profile configuration and standard pnpm verification coverage, but its original writable paths omitted both shared seams
deviations.resolution: Authorize only config.go, its loader/schema tests, the three profile schemas, the root UI package manifest, and the shell Vitest config for non-sensitive Session policy assembly and IAM test inclusion; kernel, unrelated configuration, and other packages remain out of scope

deviations.reason: The precreated IAM package manifests expose and verify only Session, so the approved Administration public slice cannot be consumed or included in standard pnpm verification
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the two IAM package manifests for the Administration public export, aggregate test/typecheck scripts, and direct @go-admin/ui dependency, plus the matching workspace lock importer; T-07 owns the lock before T-11 and may not add external versions, kernel, or composition changes

deviations.reason: The precreated Audit package manifests lack the direct canonical client and Vue dependencies, public subpath, and standard test/typecheck gates required by the approved vertical slice
deviations.resolution: Authorize the two Audit package manifests now using existing dependencies including @go-admin/ui; the shared lock remains unauthorized for T-11 until T-07 result, a Lead-owned Ticket amendment, and rebase, after which only the matching Audit importers may be opened

deviations.reason: T-06 keeps the only generic CSRF mutation fence private, while T-07 HTTP must preserve the same opaque token, CSRF, idle-touch, rotation, and failure semantics without reading Session private tables
deviations.resolution: Authorize only session/service.go and the existing session/session_test.go to add and prove a public AuthorizeRequest seam; Session schema, cookie and policy contracts, HTTP transport, and secret representations remain unchanged

deviations.reason: Audit owns a synchronous LoginRecorder but T-06 Session has no injectable call seam, so the current implementation cannot produce real login facts or satisfy AC-016 event-to-UI without a precise shared-path correction
deviations.resolution: After T-07 result and a Lead-owned T-11 rebase, authorize only session/service.go and the existing session/session_test.go for a module-neutral Login Fact Port and atomic success/failure tests; Session must not import Audit or expose username, password, token, CSRF, raw request, schema, HTTP, cookie, or policy changes, and operation events must use Audit-owned module-neutral topics rather than future Demo-private topics

deviations.reason: The precreated Demo package manifests lack canonical client, shared UI, Vue, public exports, and standard checks, while the root verify configuration does not discover Demo tests and the lock lacks Demo importers
deviations.resolution: Authorize the two Demo package manifests, Demo-only root aggregate scripts, and Demo-only Vitest includes now; after T-11 result and rebase, authorize only the two Demo lock importers using existing catalog versions, with all other importers, shared UI, composition, and external dependency versions unchanged

deviations.reason: The precreated Organization package manifests lack direct dependencies and standard checks, and ADR-012 requires an IAM consumer-defined Organization projection Port that does not yet exist
deviations.resolution: Authorize the two Organization package manifests and exact iam/administration/organization_port.go now; keep root verify, Vitest configuration, and lock read-only until T-11 and T-14 results, then amend only Organization checks and importers using existing catalog versions

deviations.reason: The fixed review proved that a production discard default can silently issue Sessions without login facts, while four existing non-Audit test call sites require an explicit test-only replacement and the required browser fixture does not exercise real rotation
deviations.resolution: Make Session construction fail closed without an explicit Login Fact Port; authorize only four exact test files for local test noops, correct the Audit browser fixture, and use a movable clock to prove real IAM replacement Cookie and CSRF propagation without changing production composition outside T-17

deviations.reason: Independent review proved Demo bypasses real IAM and its Permission Codes cannot be assigned because IAM owns the catalog tables and exposes no module registration seam
deviations.resolution: Authorize only authorization/permission_registry.go and permission_registry_test.go for a generic dual-dialect transactional registry that validates and idempotently inserts module Permission Codes and grants them to the protected system administrator; Demo owns declarations/adapters/harness and may not write IAM tables directly, while IAM schema, Session, Administration, composition, and other modules remain unchanged

deviations.reason: T-09 review proved Permission registration alone leaves business navigation unregistrable because iam_menus and iam_role_menus are also IAM-owned and no production composition seam exists
deviations.resolution: Supersede the T14-D02 file names with authorization/capability_registry.go and capability_registry_test.go and extend the same atomic dual-dialect registry to validated protected module menus plus protected system-admin grants; modules declare stable capabilities, while IAM schema, Session, Administration, composition, and direct cross-module table writes remain forbidden

deviations.reason: Independent review proved Demo duplicated the shared list request state machine, while the shared controller committed query state before request success and could not preserve the last successful projection after local validation
deviations.resolution: Authorize only go-admin-plus-ui/packages/ui/src/list.ts and tests/shell/list-form.spec.ts for synchronous normalization and validation plus latest-success atomic query/projection commits; Demo must configure and wrap the shared controller and may not retain a second list state machine

deviations.reason: T-09 stage 1 package-local checks cannot enter standard pnpm verification and its importers remain absent after the serialized T-14 lock owner completed
deviations.resolution: After rebasing to the T-14 result, authorize only Organization aggregate checks in the root package, Organization specs in shell Vitest, and the two Organization lock importers using existing catalog versions; all other root scripts, includes, importers, shared UI, IAM capability registry, and composition remain unchanged

deviations.reason: ADR-011 and T-16 require a Desktop runtime adapter, but T-05 only precreated its manifest and the T-16 writable paths omitted the reserved adapter package
deviations.resolution: Authorize only go-admin-plus-ui/packages/adapters/desktop/** for the Desktop runtime adapter; root aggregate checks and lock remain read-only during stage 1 and will be considered only after the T-09 serialized root owner completes

deviations.reason: The precreated Generator package manifests are placeholder shells without the direct dependencies, public exports, and package-local checks required by the approved Web wizard slice
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the two Generator package manifests using existing workspace and catalog dependencies; root aggregate checks and lock remain read-only during stage 1 and will be serialized after the T-09 root owner completes

deviations.reason: The precreated Settings package manifests are placeholder shells without the direct dependencies, public exports, and package-local checks required by the approved Web vertical slice
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the two Settings package manifests during stage 1 using existing workspace and catalog dependencies; root aggregate checks, Vitest include, lockfile, shared UI, and composition remain read-only until a later Lead-serialized amendment

deviations.reason: T-16 stage 1 cannot enter standard pnpm verification and its existing Desktop lock importers do not reflect the completed Tauri App and adapter dependencies after the serialized T-09 root owner finished
deviations.resolution: After a clean stage-1 commit and rebase to the amendment parent, authorize only Desktop aggregate checks in the root package, Desktop specs in shell Vitest, and the existing admin-desktop and adapter-desktop lock importers; all other root scripts, includes, importers, catalog entries, external versions, shared UI, and composition remain unchanged

deviations.reason: The precreated Scheduler package manifests cannot expose or verify the approved typed registry and Web vertical slice, while T-08 provides one global Scheduler/Outbox lease rather than independent namespace leases
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the two Scheduler package manifests for package-local exports, direct dependencies, and checks; require Scheduler and Outbox to consume the same injected global lease and transaction boundary; keep root checks, Vitest, lockfile, composition, Outbox, and coordination implementations read-only

deviations.reason: The precreated Files package manifests and Browser runtime adapter lack the exports and streaming transfer implementation required by the approved Web vertical slice
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the two Files package manifests plus Browser Files implementation/test, one export, and package-local dependency/check; keep root checks, Vitest, lockfile, shared UI, Desktop native bridge, typed Server config, and product composition read-only until serialized amendments

deviations.reason: The shared workspace boundary test hard-codes the Browser adapter dependency object to platform alone, contradicting T13-D01's approved Browser Files dependency and causing the otherwise clean root verification to fail
deviations.resolution: Authorize only go-admin-plus-ui/tests/shell/workspace-boundary.test.mjs to require the exact approved Browser adapter internal dependency set of platform plus domain-files and to reject any additional @go-admin dependency; root package, Vitest config, lockfile, shared UI, Desktop adapter, typed config, and composition remain read-only

deviations.reason: T-17 product preflight proved Audit declares permission constants but never registers permissions or a menu with the IAM-owned Module Capability Registry, so the protected system administrator cannot receive the completed Audit capability
deviations.resolution: Reopen T-11 only for Audit-owned capabilities.go and focused tests that register read/cleanup permissions plus the read-gated Audit menu through the existing registry; Session, Outbox, Audit data behavior, frontend, root manifests, lockfile, and composition remain unchanged

deviations.reason: The precreated app-shell manifest exposes only its core entry point and has no package-local check for the T-17 product manifest, while opening Apps, adapters, Rust, root aggregation, or module internals before the composition failure baseline would make shared ownership unauditable
deviations.resolution: Stage 1 authorizes only the app-shell package manifest product subpath export and package-local checks in addition to T-17 exclusive product paths; Apps, Browser/Desktop adapters, Rust bridge, root package/Vitest/lock, module implementations, and central contract tooling remain read-only until evidence-backed serialized amendments

deviations.reason: The T-17 product migration matrix fails for both SQLite and PostgreSQL because the completed Generator provider still publishes a +goose Down section, which violates the forward-only atomic migration contract enforced by the platform runner
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the SQLite and PostgreSQL 6400000000000_generator_configs.sql files to remove their Down directive and DROP statement; all other Generator implementation, schema meaning, migration version/content, module paths, root manifests, lockfile, Apps, adapters, Rust, and composition dependencies remain unchanged

deviations.reason: The clean stage-1 product checkpoint proves Web remains a placeholder, Browser rejects real dot-separated Permission Codes, Desktop UI/TypeScript/Rust/sidecar expose only Demo, and the shared product manifest is not consumed by either App
deviations.resolution: Stage 2 authorizes only the app-shell product workspace, two App composition entries, Browser permission parser, Desktop transport adapter and Rust product allowlist/proxy, desktop-sidecar product runtime wiring, plus exact package/Vitest/boundary/lock importer updates required to compile and verify those seams; domain and web-domain business implementations, generated module contracts, unrelated root scripts/importers, and final E2E remain unchanged

deviations.reason: The stage-2 aggregate test proves the platform PermissionCode type and its Web runtime fixture still encode the removed colon convention while the IAM registry, module contracts, database capabilities, product OpenAPI, and both runtime adapters use canonical dot-separated codes
deviations.resolution: Authorize only packages/platform/src/index.ts and tests/shell/web-runtime.spec.ts to replace colon Permission Codes with canonical dot-separated module.resource.action values; dual-format parsing, compatibility aliases, unrelated platform contracts, and other shell tests remain forbidden

deviations.reason: The full TypeScript aggregate gate proves tests/shell/app-shell.spec.ts is a second direct compile-time consumer of PermissionCode and its five legacy colon literals no longer typecheck after T17-D04
deviations.resolution: Authorize only tests/shell/app-shell.spec.ts to replace its five colon Permission literals with canonical dot-separated values; shell behavior, assertions, runtime implementation, and all other fixtures remain unchanged

deviations.reason: The T-19 release sidecar environment maps x86_64 only to darwin-amd64 and hard-codes Unix executable paths, so a Windows installer built solely from T-20 release assets cannot start the complete packaged Generator
deviations.resolution: Authorize only go-admin-plus-ui/apps/admin-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs to select the release toolchain by OS plus architecture, require packaged Windows Go/Node/pnpm/MinGit, pass only the bounded Windows bootstrap environment, and add matching tests; product transport, vault, lifecycle, other Desktop files, and existing macOS behavior remain unchanged

deviations.reason: Post-cutover source comparison proved ProductWorkspace and LoginPage had replaced the established admin UI/CSS despite the user's execution constraint to preserve page design while removing only deleted functions
deviations.resolution: Restore the established shared tokens, dark collapsible sidebar, 50px navbar, breadcrumb, 40px visited tabs, responsive drawer, terminal-stage login and matching source contracts in the current pnpm boundaries; do not restore captcha, legacy routes, stores, imports, Element Plus coupling, or any deleted business capability

deviations.reason: A second baseline audit proved T05-D04 restored the shell and login composition but left retained management pages with English labels, temporary green palette overrides, 20px shell padding, and inconsistent search, table, editor, action, and pagination presentation
deviations.resolution: Localize retained routes and management pages, remove obsolete scoped palette overrides, restore the established 12px page-container spacing and dense management presentation through the shared UI theme, correct the Web development port, and add static visual contracts without restoring deleted features or compatibility paths

deviations.reason: A third interaction audit proved retained CRUD pages had replaced the established toolbar plus create/edit dialog workflow with permanently visible editors, while paused browser and native drivers still targeted superseded English labels and the Scheduler page could not close a successful dialog because its settle helper discarded command results
deviations.resolution: Restore explicit toolbar actions and bounded create/edit dialogs across IAM, Organization, Demo, Settings, and Scheduler; clear cancelled form state, localize displayed enums, return Scheduler command results, synchronize paused browser/native drivers, and add static visual contracts without Element Plus, compatibility paths, restored deleted capabilities, or execution of deferred E2E

deviations.reason: A fourth exact-CSS comparison proved the historical visible TagsView was 34px and sidebar entries were 50px, while T05-D04 had encoded 40px tabs and current domain-scoped styles still overrode the shared compact 20px/34px page contract with 24px padding, width caps, 40px controls, and collapsed table styling
deviations.resolution: Restore the exact 50px sidebar entry and 34px TagsView dimensions, align the content viewport to the resulting 84px header stack, restore omitted established token names, remove domain-scoped base-control/table/page-surface overrides, and add static anti-regression coverage without changing routes, controllers, permissions, deleted capabilities, or executing deferred E2E

deviations.reason: A fifth baseline interaction audit proved LoginPage had dropped password visibility, terminal output timing, exact terminal dimensions, and a responsive breakpoint, while AccountPage had flattened the established identity-summary plus profile/password tabs and removed password confirmation despite AC-012 retaining profile, avatar metadata, and password management
deviations.resolution: Restore the retained login interactions and exact terminal presentation, rebuild AccountPage around the established summary and tabs using only current profile fields, reject mismatched password confirmation before the controller, normalize optional avatar metadata clearing, and add static and unit regressions without restoring captcha, legacy account fields, avatar upload compatibility, Element Plus, or deferred E2E

deviations.reason: A sixth retained-page interaction audit proved destructive confirmations remained in English, Settings routed non-destructive saves through deletion confirmation, Audit detail used an inconsistent native dialog, Settings and Generator hid later pages of real paginated projections, and Generator retained a stale preview-file index across restart or a new preview
deviations.resolution: Localize generic and domain-specific destructive confirmation, invoke Settings confirmation only for stable delete target kinds, move Audit detail into the shared accessible management-dialog contract with focus restoration, expose every Settings and Generator pagination controller, reset Generator preview selection at lifecycle boundaries, and add unit/static regressions without changing APIs, permissions, deleted capabilities, compatibility paths, or executing deferred E2E

deviations.reason: A seventh AC-035/source-to-contract audit proved five paginated projections hid page-size control, Files hid supported sorting, Demo could only force ascending sort, Files displayed updatedAt under a createdAt sort contract, raw transport timestamps and Scheduler task keys leaked to the UI, Settings validation erased input and lacked native constraints and busy locks, and Generator and Demo lacked existing domain-native validation constraints
deviations.resolution: Restore complete retained pagination, accessible bidirectional sorting, contract-aligned Files time semantics, localized time and task labels, failure-preserving Settings forms and native contract validation and busy locks, and Generator and Demo native validation; add static regressions without API, controller, permission, deleted capability, compatibility, or E2E changes

deviations.reason: The final documentation audit proved both project-owned Agent Skills still instructed future changes to use removed backend, frontend, authorization, migration, and composition patterns, while compatibility-zero and docs-check did not scan the skill directory
deviations.resolution: Rewrite both skills against the current dual-dialect OpenAPI, IAM capability, pnpm domain/Web Domain, shared controller, and product-composition architecture; add .agents/skills to compatibility-zero and docs-check with a regression proving stale skill content is rejected, without changing product behavior or executing deferred E2E

deviations.reason: The full-repository governance audit proved two Compose runtime .gitignore files remained after the frontend and backend cleanup, while governance-check scanned only those two source subtrees and therefore could not enforce repository-wide root ownership
deviations.resolution: After the T-18 implementation result, transfer only deploy/compose/runtime/.gitignore and deploy/compose/runtime/secrets/.gitignore to T-21, move their runtime and secret ignore rules into the root .gitignore, delete both nested files, and expand governance-check across the product repository while pruning managed tooling and generated output

deviations.reason: The AC-029 completion audit proved compatibility-zero scanned only selected governance and documentation roots and omitted JWT, refresh token, AutoMigrate, and GORM, so a new product source file could restore removed architecture while the gate remained green
deviations.resolution: Scan all repository text source and lock formats while pruning Speculo history, Git data, generated output, dependencies, and binary files; add the four missing forbidden categories and an exact path-plus-category allowlist only for license attribution, security rejection, negative tests, and release policy assertions, with Go and Rust regression probes

deviations.reason: The final repository audit proved the backend still declared the pre-reconstruction short module path go-admin and all internal imports retained it, while AC-029 explicitly requires old module paths to reach zero and compatibility-zero did not scan .mod files or reject that path
deviations.resolution: Adopt github.com/NAMEWTA/go-admin-plus/go-admin-plus as the canonical backend module, mechanically migrate every current source, test, fixture, and Generator template import, document and assert the exact declaration, scan .mod files, and reject both historical declarations and imports without adding aliases, replace directives, compatibility shims, or product behavior changes

deviations.reason: The final cross-language naming audit proved all pnpm workspace packages, lock importers, source imports, task and release filters, OpenAPI generation, and Generator templates retained the historical @go-admin/* scope despite the no-compatibility product rename and canonical @go-admin-plus/workspace identity
deviations.resolution: Atomically migrate every active workspace package and consumer to @go-admin-plus/*, make the frontend generation wrapper delegate the single root OpenAPI generator instead of a nonexistent package, assert the exact workspace and package scope, and reject the historical scope without aliases, dual scopes, compatibility shims, or behavior changes

deviations.reason: The non-E2E completion audit executed every local package target and proved Web built into a temporary Admin Web directory while archiving a nonexistent workspace dist directory, and Desktop omitted the required custom-protocol feature before attempting every configured bundle, so both public package paths failed despite narrower builds passing
deviations.resolution: Build Web directly into an artifacts-owned staging dist and atomically archive that exact output; select the supported local Desktop bundle from GOHOSTOS, require custom-protocol, retain protected DMG and signed platform packaging in their release workflows, accept the canonical Tauri 2 build-dependency manifest form, and add a workspace regression without changing UI or product behavior

deviations.reason: The final command and documentation audit proved the Web development guide promised a local Server connection and every generated client used relative /api URLs, but the Admin Web Vite server had no proxy, so task dev TARGET=web sent API requests to port 5173 instead of the Server on port 8080; command surfaces also had no regression rejecting filters for nonexistent workspace packages
deviations.resolution: Add a fixed loopback /api development proxy without path rewriting, load the actual Vite config in the workspace boundary suite, scan root Task/CI/script/release/deploy command surfaces against all 25 real workspace manifests, and document current build/package outputs and protected release ownership without changing UI, CSS, product behavior, or executing deferred E2E

deviations.reason: The completion audit proved the current SpecDev runtime verification config still invoked the removed frontend directory and legacy Make build, while the D09/D10 repository-root package and command assertions were placed in a workspace suite that the Generator intentionally copies without root Task or scripts, causing the canonical real-generation test to fail after 190.97 seconds
deviations.resolution: Point SpecDev verification at the canonical root Task command plane and current pnpm workspace; make architecture-check enforce those exact commands, all workspace filters, and local packaging contracts; keep the independently copied workspace suite self-contained, with negative root regressions and full normal/SQLite Generator verification, without skipping checks or changing UI, CSS, product behavior, or deferred E2E

deviations.reason: The final verification-coverage audit proved the root frontend typecheck manually omitted three packages that declared typecheck and six of ten test projects, while the central Vitest allowlist omitted eight unit spec files and the standard task test command omitted 29 Node unit tests for browser/native harness diagnostics and lifecycle helpers
deviations.resolution: Run every declared workspace typecheck recursively, compile every discovered test tsconfig, discover every package and harness unit spec, add a self-contained Node unit-test runner under the Generator-copied shell skeleton, and enforce all four coverage contracts in the root architecture gate without running E2E or changing UI, CSS, product behavior, contracts, schema, or release behavior

deviations.reason: The final build-completeness audit proved task build TARGET=desktop compiled only Vite WebView assets, while TARGET=all built only the Server command plus Web/Desktop assets and omitted both the host Go sidecar and Rust/Tauri executable despite current documentation and Evidence describing complete Server/sidecar/Web/Desktop builds
deviations.resolution: Make the Desktop build stage the approved host sidecar and run a custom-protocol Tauri release build with --no-bundle; route both desktop and all through that native build, keep package/signing/notarization in the existing package and protected release commands, document the macOS/Windows host constraint, and enforce the build wiring in architecture tests without running E2E

deviations.reason: The final CI build-completeness audit proved the macOS Desktop job staged the Go sidecar but did not install the frozen pnpm workspace and ended with cargo check, so CI never ran the Tauri CLI beforeBuildCommand or linked the release Desktop executable that the canonical local build now requires
deviations.resolution: Install the pinned pnpm workspace in the Desktop CI job, retain sidecar staging plus locked Rust tests and strict clippy, replace release cargo check with custom-protocol Tauri build --no-bundle, and enforce all three job-local contracts in the architecture gate without bundling, signing, publishing, changing product behavior, or running E2E

deviations.reason: The final local command-plane audit proved a Volta-launched Node runner removed its sibling pnpm shim from child PATH, so canonical root frontend tasks failed even though pnpm 11.1.3 was installed; directly invoking Corepack fixed only the outer command because nested workspace scripts still could not resolve pnpm
deviations.resolution: Prefer an installed pnpm command, otherwise generate a standard Corepack pnpm shim under the ignored root artifacts directory, export it for nested package scripts, route every root frontend task through one resolver with exact exec status propagation, enforce the routing in architecture and Task contract tests, and document the current setup without changing product behavior or running E2E

deviations.reason: The final cold-start audit proved the repository did not declare Go Task as a root command dependency or distinguish language minimums from CI verification baselines, so a local success could not be reconstructed deterministically
deviations.resolution: Require exact Go Task 3.48.0, document manifest-owned Go, Node, pnpm, and Rust minimums separately from CI baselines, and enforce the Task, Node, pnpm, and Rust declarations across CI, the command contract, README, and development guide without introducing a legacy version matrix

deviations.reason: A real full task test under the unmodified Volta environment proved the Go generator's Node child still failed with spawnSync pnpm ENOENT, while an unversioned Corepack call from the repository root selected pnpm 10.34.5 instead of the workspace's required 11.1.3
deviations.resolution: Share one exact pnpm 11.1.3 resolver across backend and frontend scripts, prepare its inherited shim before server tests, development, and contract generation, install the frozen cross-language generator workspace in backend CI, reject direct version drift, and preserve deterministic failure and exit propagation without compatibility fallback

deviations.reason: The final AC-011/AC-022 audit proved the Web runtime omitted IAM dataScope and the Shell widened a missing scope to all, while two real concurrent Go test runs proved the Generator could fail through the Volta Node shim with Resource temporarily unavailable even though the isolated 339-second generation gate passed
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the twelve recorded product runtime, shared platform, Web/Desktop adapter, Shell regression, and Generator resolver files; require one explicit self-or-all identity contract with no compatibility default, resolve Volta to its installed Node runtime for deterministic concurrent generation, and leave UI/CSS, modular OpenAPI, schema, migrations, removed capabilities, protected release, and deferred E2E unchanged

deviations.reason: The final production-artifact audit proved Vite removed the native E2E JavaScript branch but retained its scoped native-e2e CSS in the Desktop production bundle, while the existing restore check searched only one visible button label and therefore could not prove that production assets contained no test controls
deviations.resolution: Move native test controls into a dedicated native-e2e build entry selected only by an explicit Vite mode, keep the production App limited to ProductWorkspace composition, make every Desktop production build byte-scan all emitted assets for native control routes and markers, reuse that verifier during native artifact restoration, and leave product UI/CSS, runtime behavior, protected release, and deferred E2E unchanged

deviations.reason: The follow-up production boundary audit proved the new WebView verifier listed only five selected native control strings while the production sidecar and host restore path still scanned only the test-control route, leaving the remaining boundary, authorization, fixture, environment, and feature markers outside one authoritative rejection contract
deviations.resolution: Define one immutable marker set covering the route, build modes, environment and feature identities, all E2E messages, and fixture prefixes; apply it to both emitted WebView trees and explicit production binaries; require functional rejection tests for every marker and static proof that native restoration uses the shared file verifier; leave product code, UI/CSS, database, public contracts, and deferred E2E unchanged

deviations.reason: The final production-build audit proved D20 scanned sidecar and host binaries only while the paused native runner restored artifacts; canonical local build and package, Desktop CI, and protected macOS and Windows release paths could complete without applying the shared production marker contract to their final binaries
deviations.resolution: Add one cross-platform verifier that derives exact host and sidecar paths from the existing target-triple contract; invoke it after local Desktop build and package and in Desktop CI, scan the protected macOS and Windows host and sidecar before signing or staging, replace collision-prone four-byte wildcard markers with exact current test-control strings, and enforce all wiring with negative architecture and release-policy tests without running E2E

deviations.reason: The final Spec-to-source adapter audit proved CONTEXT requires Browser and Desktop Runtime Adapters to implement the Platform Port and the Spec requires Desktop file selection/download, clipboard, and notification host capabilities, but PlatformPort is declaration-only, both adapters omit it, product composition does not inject it, and Desktop Files still relies on browser DOM file and download behavior
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the existing platform, Browser/Desktop adapter, dual App composition, shared Files page, Tauri host capability/permission/dependency, focused frontend test, workspace manifest/lock, and architecture gate paths needed to implement one explicit PlatformPort; keep Web file-input presentation unchanged, route Desktop file pick/save through bounded custom Rust commands without exposing native paths or generic filesystem access, expose write-only clipboard and notification operations, and leave business APIs, databases, removed capabilities, visible product styling, protected release, and deferred E2E unchanged

deviations.reason: The post-D22 binary data-path audit proved the Files OpenAPI response always emits Content-Type application/octet-stream while the Desktop Rust proxy accepts only image/png, image/jpeg, application/pdf, and text/plain for a successful Files content response, so every Desktop download is rejected before the shared Files page can save it
deviations.resolution: Authorize only the Desktop Rust proxy and unit tests, Desktop adapter and focused tests, and the corresponding SpecDev/architecture evidence needed to enforce one exact application/octet-stream binary envelope with canonical bounded base64 and no extra IPC fields; do not add MIME compatibility branches or change Files API, OpenAPI, database, page markup, UI/CSS, protected release, or deferred E2E

deviations.reason: The final Desktop source-graph audit proved src-tauri/src/demo_contract.rs remains as a 525-line unreferenced pre-product contract after T-17 cut over main.rs and proxy.rs to product_contract.rs; Cargo never compiles its tests or validators, and it alone keeps time and uuid as direct Desktop dependencies
